title: MyGo: Consistent and Controllable Multi-View Driving Video Generation with Camera Control

output_modality.value: multi-view driving video (8-frame clips at 256x512, 6 views on nuScenes); also single-view camera-controlled video on RealEstate10K

control_signal.value: onboard camera pose (intrinsics, extrinsics, as Plucker embeddings) to control ego motion, plus BEV map, 3D boxes, first-frame keyframes and neighbour-view video

control_mechanism.value: ControlNet-like module injecting Plucker coordinates before temporal transformers with zero-initialised linear layers; other conditions via condition cross-attention; epipolar-masked neighbour-view cross-attention

base_model.value: pre-trained Stable Video Diffusion image-to-video latent diffusion U-Net with pre-trained VAE, original transformer frozen during training, Diffusers codebase

datasets.value: nuScenes (700 train, 150 validation scenes) and RealEstate10K (all training samples; 1000 random evaluation samples)

metrics.value: FID, FVD, RotErr and TransErr (COLMAP-based, RealEstate10K only), KPM score for multi-view consistency on nuScenes

controllability_evidence.value: RealEstate10K: MyGo RotErr 7.71 and TransErr 5.98 versus CameraCtrl 8.36 and 6.27. nuScenes KPM 81.22% versus 80.67% (CameraCtrl); FID 11.60, FVD 122.06.

closed_loop.value: no; open-loop video generation of short clips (8 frames at 2 frames per second), no policy in the loop

stated_limitations.value: Ego motion is mostly forward or backward with large displacement, so epipolar constraints and rule-based consistency are hard to apply; first-frame conditioning is not enough for some scenarios (sentence cut off in packet).

notes: Camera control accuracy is verified only on RealEstate10K, since COLMAP fails on dynamic nuScenes scenes; nuScenes controllability is via KPM consistency. Limitation sentence truncated.
